```python
def record(item, bucket=[]):
    bucket.append(item)
    return bucket
```
Explain the actual behavior accurately, then provide a version with a fresh list by default that still accepts an explicit list."

The issue is the classic Python mutable default argument problem. The default argument `bucket=[]` is evaluated once when the function is defined, not each time the function is called. So the same list object is shared across all calls that don't provide an explicit bucket argument.

- This is the standard correct fix
